verdict.reason: The code observation is literally true (the signature matches verbatim and probe_depth_convention never overrides the defaults), but the finding's normative core is a misattribution of two different tests. PROTOCOL declares itself the referee for Phases 3 and 4 only (line 3), and its single depth-convention threshold, in 4.1, governs a Phase 4 test on VGGT depth: a per-pixel ratio of resampled VGGT depth to ground-truth depth regressed against the secant of the pixel angle. classify_depth_convention is the Phase 1 Habitat renderer test required by CLAUDE.md, and it computes an entirely different statistic (robust residual spread of the depth map about a fitted affine plane, versus the same after dividing by the ray-norm map) on a different input (the renderer's raw depth, with no VGGT and no ground-truth reference). A repo-wide grep for a secant or slope regression returns nothing in src/ or tests/, confirming the 4.1 test does not exist yet and therefore no code currently reads or should read that protocol constant. Consequently flat_tol, margin, center_crop, and max_samples are not among "the numeric constants this protocol references," and the preamble's configs/analysis.yaml requirement does not reach render_replica.py:283. The absence of configs/analysis.yaml is real and serious, but it is a standalone repo-level gap already designated the first blocker by VALIDATION.md line 13; pinning it to a Phase 1 function converts a genuine missing-artifact blocker into a spurious per-line violation. Severity is also unsupportable on its own terms: the Phase 1 thresholds are not silently applied, since every probe's stats are persisted to classification.json, the verdict is written to manifest metadata, and manifest validation raises on an unresolved verdict or non-planar stored depth (lines 608-614), so the decision is auditable after the fact regardless of where the constants live.

verdict.reason: The auditor's mechanical sub-claims all check out: the evidence is verbatim at 1187-1189, probe_depth_convention (line 1138) passes only two positional arguments so the defaults at 282-285 always apply, RenderConfig (895-934) declares no matching field, and load_config (950-960) raises on unknown yaml keys. The finding is nonetheless refuted because both protocol references are misapplied to the wrong depth-convention test. PROTOCOL.md:5 constrains only "numeric constants this protocol references," and PROTOCOL.md:3 scopes the document to Phases 3 and 4; the sole depth-convention threshold it references is at 4.1 (line 107), a Phase 4 regression of the VGGT-over-ground-truth depth ratio against the secant of the off-axis angle. classify_depth_convention is a categorically different procedure - a robust plane-residual-spread comparison on raw Habitat renderer output - and belongs to the Phase 1 requirement in CLAUDE.md ("Phase 1 includes a test that determines whether the renderer outputs planar z-depth or euclidean ray distance, and converts if needed"), which imposes no config requirement at all. VALIDATION.md 1.6 is worse as a citation: it is headed "Masks," names the co-visibility depth tolerance, and directs the grep at the visibility module; it is not a general config-read rule and never mentions the renderer. VALIDATION.md 2.6 is the section that does cover depth conventions, and it draws exactly the distinction the finding collapses - the renderer's test need only be re-run with its metadata confirmed, while only the VGGT secant regression carries "the config-frozen threshold." Two further points cut against the finding as written. First, the code is not a silent tunable: the probe requires at least three mutually agreeing confident verdicts (1192), raises RuntimeError on all-ambiguous or disagreeing probes (1197-1206), persists classification.json, and records raw_verdict and converted_to_planar in run metadata (1208-1215), which is precisely the behavior VALIDATION 2.6 asks of the renderer's test; and the constants are pinned by positive and negative tests at tests/test_render_replica.py:248-271 and 274-299, where structureless and mostly-invalid maps must return "ambiguous," so a moved threshold breaks the suite. Second, the auditor's own premise is unavailable: configs/analysis.yaml does not exist on disk and has no git history, so no constant anywhere in this repo is currently config-frozen. The defensible finding in this area is the missing normative artifact - which VALIDATION.md:13 calls the first blocker - not a per-function hard-coding in an out-of-scope Phase 1 probe. Severity drops from minor to note: worth recording as an undocumented constant, not as a protocol violation.

def load_config(path: Path) -> RenderConfig:
    """Load a RenderConfig from yaml. Unknown keys are an error, not a warning."""
    import yaml

    raw = yaml.safe_load(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"config {path} did not parse to a mapping")
    allowed = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(RenderConfig)}
    unknown = sorted(set(raw) - allowed)
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown config keys: {unknown}")
    missing = [k for k in ("replica_root", "output_root", "scenes") if k not in raw]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"config missing required keys: {missing}")
    return RenderConfig(**raw)

Rotation is unchanged across the translation program and moves are along the base camera's x and z axes, so a static point's planar z-depth is unchanged by a lateral move and shifted by exactly the forward displacement otherwise. 1. The protocol reference is misapplied on both legs. VALIDATION.md 1.1 is scoped entirely to pose convention: it makes a duplicate a major finding only for "a second inline implementation of a relative transform or a matrix inversion of a pose." VALIDATION.md contains exactly two single-definition rules, 1.1 (relative pose) and 1.3 (the pixel-to-patch mapping constant). Neither reaches inverse-intrinsics normalization. Extending 1.1 "by analogy" invents a rule the frozen audit document does not contain, and ground rule 3 requires each finding to be a code-versus-protocol disagreement. Likewise, CLAUDE.md's "Write this formula once in geometry.py and import it everywhere" is anchored to the sentence immediately preceding it, which defines T_target_from_context; quoting it detached from that antecedent turns a specific instruction about the relative pose formula into a general anti-duplication principle it never states.

2. Both proposed remedies are unavailable as stated. geometry.unproject (geometry.py:79-94) requires a depth map and returns depth-scaled camera-frame points (x*d, y*d, d); classify_depth_convention has no trusted depth, since deciding the depth convention is precisely its job, and needs unscaled coordinates. And ray_norm_map returns only the norm, not x and y, while classify_depth_convention needs x and y as separate regressors for _plane_residual_spread(dv, xv, yv) at line 334. Neither existing function can be called here without a signature change, so "rather than sharing one helper or geometry.unproject" describes a refactor that does not exist as an available call.

3. The claim is incomplete as a single-definition audit. The same normalization appears a third time at geometry.py:92-93 inside unproject. If the argument had force, the site the auditor implicitly nominates as canonical is itself one of the copies. A repo-wide grep for the pattern returns exactly three hits, and the claim names two.

4. The only real hazard, silent drift between the copies, is already closed by the test suite. tests/test_render_replica.py:246-255 constructs euclidean depth as planar * ray_norm_map(...) and asserts classify_depth_convention returns "euclidean_ray", and test_depth_convention_tolerates_tilted_planes at lines 296-299 repeats that cross-check on tilted planes. If the inline copy at 317-319 diverged from ray_norm_map, those assertions fail. The two copies are behaviorally pinned to each other.

5. There is zero numerical consequence today: both sites use float64, the same geometry.pixel_grid, and identical arithmetic.

6. Finally, classify_depth_convention is not the PROTOCOL 4.1 depth-convention test the audit cares about; 4.1 specifies a secant regression of VGGT depth against ground truth. This is the Phase 1 renderer test, which VALIDATION 2.6 checks behaviorally ("Re-run the renderer's depth-convention test on raw output"), not structurally.

Grep for "parallax" across src/, tests/, and configs/ hits only datasets.py, figures.py, geometry.py, render_replica.py, and visibility.py; evaluate.py and correspondence.py never compute it. The stored row value is `pair.as_row()` at evaluate.py:483, and figures.py:94 reads `row["parallax"]` for the curves, so the manifest-time value is the one that reaches every parallax-stratified result. The co-visible set is computed later in `pair_geometry` (evaluate.py:472-482) and never feeds the statistic. tests/test_geometry.py:120-127 pins the frame-median definition, so the deviation is locked in by the suite. (4) The auditor's framing is partly wrong and I corrected it: since the baseline is a constant per pair and d -> b/d is monotone on positive depths, median(b/d_i) equals b/median(d_i) on the same point set (exactly for odd counts; only even-count interpolation differs, negligibly). The real and defensible deviation is the population: all valid pixels of the context depth map versus the pair's co-visible points. A consequence that makes it observable: because the denominator depends only on the context frame, the stored parallax is exactly proportional to baseline within a context frame, whereas the protocol's statistic would shift per pair as the co-visible set shrinks with viewpoint change, precisely at the large-parallax end that carries the 3.8 ceiling-decay and margin-growth claims. The quoted snippet is verbatim at 305-308, and the observable symptom is real, but the finding is misattributed and its severity is overstated on three independent grounds.

(1) Wrong locus. figures.py is purely data-driven and adds no violation of its own. paired_records drops any nonfinite metric (lines 83-87), and the plotting loop skips a series with no bins (lines 321-323). If the evaluation obeyed 3.7 — centered Mean-Feature absent or N/A, which VALIDATION.md 4.3 says may be represented "either by row absence or by an explicit N/A marker" — line 308 would draw no centered Mean-Feature curve whatsoever. tests/test_figures.py:88-94 pins exactly that degradation with a NaN Mean-Feature. So line 305 cannot plot a curve 3.7 forbids unless something upstream first computes one.

(2) The real defect is in evaluate.py and is a different finding. Line 315 uses mean_feature_map — a position-conditioned [C, Hp, Wp] map — as the Mean-Feature prediction, which PROTOCOL 3.6 explicitly forbids ("a single global D-dimensional mean vector per encoder... Position-conditioned mean maps are explicitly not used"), while line 294 centers with the global mean vector. Map minus global vector is nonzero, which is precisely why a finite centered Mean-Feature score exists at all. Separately, line 87's .clamp(min=eps) is the "epsilon-regularized zero vector" that 3.7 names and forbids, and would still manufacture a 0.0 score even after the map is corrected to a vector. Neither line is in figures.py.

(3) Severity is overstated and the issue is already recorded, not newly discovered. PROTOCOL 3.7's own Verification note (line 73) already documents that "the completed run ... reports finite centered Mean-Feature values (0.247 per-point, 0.428 splat-and-pool for DINOv2), which is impossible under this section's paired definitions," and assigns validation the job of identifying which definition diverged. VALIDATION.md 2.5 pre-classifies the outcome: "reject any finite centered Mean-Feature score as a major finding." The project's own frozen referee rates this major, in the scores, not blocker, in the figure.

Additionally the localization is incomplete even within figures.py: summary_table (lines 136-162, VARIANT_ORDER includes MEAN_FEATURE and the metric loop covers cosine_centered_mean) emits value[Mean-Feature] and margin[Mean-Feature] for the centered metric, and format_console_summary (line 258) prints it per metric via main() line 384. A blocker resting on figures.py would have to cite all three sites, not one.

What survives is minor: figures.py encodes no metric-aware raw-only rule for Mean-Feature, so it will not catch a regression if the corrected eval marks centering N/A with an explicit sentinel rather than absence or NaN. Worth hardening, but it is a symptom of the evaluate.py divergence, not the violation itself.

The quoted line is verbatim correct at 516, so the raw code observation stands. What is refuted is the protocol linkage that gives the finding its severity.

1. The 4.5 reference is contradicted by the section it cites. PROTOCOL 4.5 states that under zero translation the projection "reduces to the depth-free homography K_target R K_context inverse" and that estimated depth "cannot move any correspondence in the in-place rotation regime." Any positive depth value produces the identical reprojected coordinate, so float16 quantization of any magnitude is exactly invisible to the per-point 1e-5 gate. The auditor cites the gate as if storage precision were an input to it; the cited text says depth is not an input to it at all. The only depth-sensitive part of 4.5 is splat-and-pool collision resolution, and 4.5 already neutralizes that by forcing Oracle-Transport's collision ordering on the common-valid intersection, gating that at 1e-3, and explicitly reporting the unforced difference as the collision-ordering tax "not gated."

2. The 4.3 reference does not support a precision concern either. 4.3's Level 1 and Level 2 estimators are medians of a depth ratio pooled over all valid pixels of whole frames, and the sensitivity row is unweighted OLS over every pre-alignment-valid pixel of an image. Both are massively-averaged estimators. float16 half-ulp relative error is at most 2^-11 = 4.9e-4, roughly 2 mm at 2 m and 4 mm at 4-8 m, which is two orders of magnitude below real VGGT depth error and more than an order below the repo's own 1.5 percent co-visibility tolerance. 4.3's one stated inviolable rule is target exclusion, not numeric precision.

3. PROTOCOL.md imposes no storage-precision requirement anywhere: grep for float, precision, dtype, fp16, half, and quantiz returns zero matches in the whole document. There is therefore no protocol-implementation disagreement to record, which is the standard PROTOCOL.md sets for a validation finding.

4. The precision estimate is overstated on its upper end. "millimeters to centimeters" at "a few meters" is wrong at the centimeter end: float16 ulp only reaches 1 cm above roughly 16 m, which is out of range for Replica indoor scenes. The realistic figure is 2-4 mm.

5. This is not an unnoticed fact needing to be "recorded." def _write_npz(path: Path, arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray]) -> None:
    """Write an npz through a temporary file, then rename it into place.

    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with open(tmp, "wb") as handle:

    os.replace(tmp, path)

Writing meta.json last is standard commit-last ordering; meta.json is the marker that says "this cache is finished," which is precisely why the guard keys on it. Two independent call sites depend on that meaning: encoders.py:867-871, where --resume skips a scene only if CACHE_META_NAME exists, and scripts/run_phase2_cache.sh:86, which builds the SLURM array from scenes lacking meta.json. Keying the guard on features.npz as well would make an interrupted run permanently unrunnable without manual deletion — strictly worse, and it would break both resume paths.

3. Nothing recoverable is lost. The overwritten file is an orphan from a run that already failed, replaced by a re-encode of the same frames by the same frozen encoder under eval/no_grad. There is also no silent-read risk: an archive without meta.json fails load_cache_meta, so validate_feature_cache (596-634) — invoked on every cache via cache_scene (771) and via --validate-only (841-861) — reports "[scene] MISSING" and exits nonzero rather than treating it as complete.

4. The protocol reference does not say what the finding needs it to say. VALIDATION.md 1.10 covers seeds, committed configs, and "outputs are never overwritten," which CLAUDE.md scopes to outputs/{experiment_name}/. cache/ is gitignored, derived, and regenerable, not an experiment output. Even on the broadest reading the requirement is met: finished caches raise FileExistsError (488-492), covered by test_cache_refuses_to_overwrite (163-169).

The only true residual I could construct is far narrower than the claim: if a run crashes after depth.npz is written and the operator then reruns with export_depth flipped off, a stale depth.npz remains beside a meta.json recording has_depth false, and validate_feature_cache only inspects depth when meta["has_depth"] is true (623). That leaves an unreferenced file, requires an operator config change between the two runs, and affects no result — a note at most, and not the finding as filed. Check 1.10 passes on this code.

Second, two of the three "absent" items are not lost information: meta.json records "encoder": encoder.spec.name at line 534, which is the key into the module-level ENCODERS table at lines 172-201, where source and normalization are version-controlled constants that git already pins to the commit that produced the cache.
